headline: Tempus swings to a profit as revenue growth accelerates
summary_short: Tempus AI's Q2 2026 revenue rose 22% y/y to $382.5 million, with Diagnostics up 20% and Data and Applications up 28%; the company posted its first GAAP net income quarter at $5.6 million versus a $42.8 million loss a year ago.
summary_long: Diagnostics grew on oncology test volume (+31% to ~96,500 tests, +$37.5M) and hereditary testing; Data and Applications grew on Insights demand (+$20.5M), including the Pathos Foundation Model agreement. Cost of revenue grew only 14% against 22% revenue growth, expanding gross margin to 64.4% (+243bps). Operating loss widened to $75.9M on 25% higher SG&A ($20.9M more stock comp) and continued R&D investment. Net income turned positive mainly on a $60.7M unrealized gain on marketable securities and lower interest expense after debt prepayment. Tempus raised $460M via 0% convertible notes (net $441.9M), retiring $317.9M of term loan/revolver debt; cash rose to $599.6M. FY2026 guidance: revenue raised to $1.595-$1.605B, Adjusted EBITDA ~$65M.

drivers.explanation: Revenue growth accelerated on higher oncology/hereditary test volumes and Data and Applications demand; Tempus posted its first GAAP net income quarter, aided by a large unrealized securities gain and lower interest expense.
Diagnostics revenue rose 20% on oncology test volume growth (+$37.5M) and hereditary testing gains; Data and Applications rose 28% on Insights demand, including the Pathos Foundation Model agreement.
Cost of revenues grew 14% y/y versus 22% revenue growth, so gross margin expanded even as cloud, personnel and stock-comp costs rose in absolute dollars.
Operating loss widened as SG&A rose 25% (largely $20.9M more stock-based compensation, $14.2M more personnel costs) and R&D/tech R&D investment continued.
Net income turned positive mainly on a $60.7M unrealized gain on marketable equity securities and a 52% drop in interest expense after debt prepayments, not from core operating profitability.
Cash rose on $441.9M net proceeds from a new $460M 0% convertible note due 2032, partly offset by repaying $317.9M of term loan and revolver debt and a $31.2M capped-call purchase.
